Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (<10%) rested on a comment citing 'non-hydro 0.8%' only, which excludes hydropower; but the metadata definition of this variable explicitly counts hydro as a renewable source. The cited source (a generic World Bank country landing page with no renewable-generation figure) does not itself support a <10% score. Fetched the Ghana Energy Commission's 2025 National Energy Statistical Bulletin (energycom.gov.gh), a primary authoritative source, which reports hydropower at 39% (9,893 of 25,550 GWh) and other renewables (chiefly solar) at 0.71% of total generation in 2024, a combined renewable share of roughly 40%. Historical series in the same report shows hydro's share declining steadily from over 90% in 2000 as thermal capacity has expanded, consistent with IRENA/EIA-derived generation-mix data reviewed alongside it. Recalculated Value Code to 3 (25-49%) per the metadata scale.
revised_comments: Ghana's electricity generation mix includes a substantial renewable component driven primarily by hydropower from the Akosombo and Bui dams. Ghana Energy Commission data show hydropower supplying 39% of total electricity generation (9,893 GWh of 25,550 GWh) in 2024, with a further 0.71% from solar and other renewables, giving a combined renewable share of around 40%. This places Ghana in the 25-49% band, though the renewable share has been on a long-term declining trend as thermal generation capacity has expanded faster than hydro output and hydrological variability has constrained further hydro growth.
